label: VERIFIED
extraction: Anthropic decision framework for multi-agent systems. Multi-agent architecture: multiple LLM instances with separate conversation contexts coordinated through code. Orchestrator-subagent pattern focus: hierarchical model where lead spawns and manages specialized subagents. Observed teams build elaborate multi-agent architectures only to discover improved prompting on single agent achieved equivalent results. Common failure: lost context at handoffs, spent more tokens coordinating than executing. Multi-agent provides value when: single agent accumulates everything in context (must reason about issue while maintaining 20+ files), parallel workstreams with independent context, specialization single agent can't sustain. Managed infrastructure can handle orchestration (Claude Managed Agents). Patterns: generator-verifier, orchestrator-subagent, agent teams. Key principle: multi-agent should be reserved for cases where they provide clear benefits justifying cost.
